scope: Proposition 16.6 (Central panel tests) of the manuscript “Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups” (preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a6c45541e6943005), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 119. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix K, a bound q on the number of target link vertices, and a bound r on the number of prescribed directions at an internal apex. There is a bound B, depending only on these bounds and the fixed original data, with the following property after suitable kernel choices. For every such target list and direction list there is a partition of the targets into classes, each in one component of LN and of intrinsic diameter at most B, such that every binary assignment to these classes extends to a central panel. Its cut germs are pairwise at angle greater than K, and all are at angle greater than K from the prescribed directions. The same partition works for all binary assignments. There are also fillers: for every occurrence of a link edge there is a panel cutting that occurrence whose cuts all lie over its one base edge in LH. Its cut germs can be required pairwise farther than K.
